requirement: Under {cite}`requirements.cli.skill_structure`, the `habeas-bootstrap-requirements` skill MUST be the home of deriving an initial requirement set from existing code.
rationale:
**Requirement.** `requirements.cli.skill_structure.bootstrap` has one obligation. The `habeas-bootstrap-requirements` skill MUST be the home of deriving an initial requirement set from existing code. Under the parent `requirements.cli.skill_structure`, that means the skill states the topic in full, and no other skill restates it.

**Implementation.** `assets/skills/habeas-bootstrap-requirements/SKILL.md` carries the {impl} reference for the whole file.
- It states the whole bootstrap topic. The Workflow covers reading the code, building the inventories, proposing, reviewing, tagging, validating and authoring, a fresh-subagent recount, and the report.
- It has the sections `## Inventories`, `## Proposing requirements`, `## Tagging` and `## Report`.
- The Inventories section covers tests, items and behavior, and the gap list. Proposing requirements labels each proposal as intended, a possible bug, or incidental. Tagging covers the roots and tests. The Report section gives the report format and the 100% claim criteria.
- It defers other topics to their homes instead of restating them: directive syntax to `habeas`; review, agreement and "Choosing references" to `habeas-requirements`; authoring and FIXME handling to `habeas-evidence`.

**Test.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_bootstrap_skill_is_home_of_deriving_an_initial_requirement_set]` carries the {test} reference.
- It reads the raw `SKILL.md` through `skill_md`. For each of the four headings above, it calls `section`, which asserts that the heading exists.
- It then calls `assert_home("habeas-bootstrap-requirements")`. That helper runs `assert_phrases` with the markers from `home_markers`: "every first-party runnable test or test case", "## Proposing requirements" and "Independent recount:". It then asserts that no other bundled skill contains any of those markers. The markers appear in the skill text I read.
- The "exactly one home" half of the parent obligation is therefore asserted. The skill states the topic, and no other skill restates it.

**Reachability and unspecified behavior.** The skill file is the single {impl} root, so all its content is reachable. The skill adds no behavior that another requirement fails to specify. The test helpers (`assert_home`, `section`, `skill_md` and others) are reached from a test marked {test}.

I found no gaps.

text: Under {cite}`requirements.cli.skill_structure`, the `habeas-bootstrap-requirements` skill MUST be the home of deriving an initial requirement set from existing code.

Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST jointly give the direction that the requirements on them specify. A skill consists of its `SKILL.md` and the files under its `references/` directory. Each topic MUST be stated in full in exactly one skill, its home.
